claims.text: A page exists in the Pulumi docs at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ (the link target of the 'Provider support policy' card on the support index).
The Pulumi docs page 'Provider support policy' describes how long Pulumi maintains each provider major version.
Pulumi provides long-term security updates for some providers, and the Provider support policy page states which providers get them.
Pulumi focuses on actively supporting the latest released major version of the providers it maintains.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version for up to a year, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The Pulumi provider support policy page at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ exists and lists the covered providers and what a long-term support release contains.
Pulumi provider major versions older than the previous major (for providers covered by long-term support) and older majors of other providers receive no patches at all.
The current version of all providers maintained by Pulumi can be found in the Pulumi Registry at /registry/.
Pulumi experimental features are always opt-in, enabled with a flag, command, or environment variable such as PULUMI_EXPERIMENTAL=true; they can change or be removed without a deprecation cycle.
Pulumi does not automatically roll back changes during an update if an error occurs; it completes pending in-progress operations, then exits and reports the error.
Pulumi does not automatically query the cloud provider's live state before running `pulumi up` or `pulumi preview`.
`pulumi up --refresh` refreshes state and applies the desired state in a single step.
Pulumi Cloud provides built-in drift detection for scheduled automated drift detection and remediation.
Pulumi auto-naming appends a random suffix to the logical name and lets Pulumi create replacement resources before deleting old ones.
Pulumi Cloud manages a unique encryption key per stack, configurable to use a custom secrets provider, so encrypting the same value in different stacks yields different ciphertext.
Pulumi does not use the Terraform engine; some Pulumi providers use Terraform schemas, while Pulumi native providers map directly to cloud provider APIs and do not use Terraform schemas.
In npm, the tilde operator (~1.2.3) allows patch updates on the current minor version.
Each major version of a Pulumi provider includes migration logic to smooth upgrade from the immediately previous major version, but these migrations do not always work across multiple major versions.
Pulumi actively maintains the latest released major version of every provider it publishes.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version for up to 12 months, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The providers that receive long-term support updates on eligible older versions are: AWS, Azure Classic, Azure Native, Azure AD, Command, Docker Build, GCP, Kubernetes, TLS, and Vault.
The Pulumi Registry has package pages at /registry/packages/aws/, azure, azure-native, azuread, command, docker-build, gcp, kubernetes, tls, and vault for the listed LTS providers.

The Pulumi provider LTS branch ships High/Critical CVE security patches: fixes for CVEs affecting the provider's code or its direct dependencies, and fixes for broken internal infrastructure on the LTS branch needed to ship them.

A Pulumi provider LTS release does not contain new upstream API versions, new resources or properties, performance improvements, non-security bug fixes, or compatibility with newer language runtime versions.
Pulumi LTS providers remain compatible with the version of the Pulumi engine they were frozen at, unless security fixes prompt otherwise.
Under the Pulumi provider support policy, exactly one long-term support major version exists per provider at any time.

When major version N+1 of a Pulumi provider ships, it becomes the new N, the old N becomes the new LTS major, and the old LTS major reaches end of life on the same day regardless of how much of its 12-month window remained.
Within the Pulumi provider LTS major version, only the latest minor version receives patches; earlier minors are frozen.
Pulumi provider LTS releases are available through the same standard package registries as current-major releases but are tagged differently.
Customers pinning to a specific major version of a Pulumi provider automatically receive patch releases as they ship, and pinning to a major version is recommended.
At any time, exactly one major version of a covered provider is the LTS version, and older majors receive no patches.
If v3 is the newest release, then v3 is N, v2 is N−1 (LTS), and v1 and earlier are end of life.
The current major (N) of a Pulumi provider receives new features, new resources, bug fixes, security patches, dependency upgrades, and new upstream API versions until N+1 ships.

The LTS major (N−1) of a covered Pulumi provider is supported for up to 12 months from N's release, or until N+1 ships, and receives security updates in the provider's code or its direct dependencies.
Pulumi provider versions N−2 and older are end of life, not supported, and will not receive updates.
The Pulumi support FAQ at /docs/support/faq/infrastructure/ has a section 'what-are-the-best-practices-for-maintaining-provider-versions'.
Pages exist at /registry/ and /docs/support/getting-support/.
